📖 Core Definitions

Essential Terminology & Concepts

Why Study Algorithms? Key Concept

In the field of Computer Science, everything is related to databases.

Categories Of Sorting Algorithms Key Concept

Sorting algorithms are generally compared on the following parameters: 1.

Bubble Sort Key Concept

Bubble sort is the simplest algorithm that works by comparing each pair of elements and swapping elements if they are in the wrong order.

Selection Sort Key Concept

Selection sort works by repeatedly selecting the smallest element from the unsorted Sorted Array Sorted Array 76 array and swapping it with the first unsorted element.

Insertion Sort Key Concept

It is a simple sorting algorithm that divide the array into two parts i.e., sorted and unsorted.

📌 Key Takeaways

Section-by-Section Study Breakdown

12.2 Why Study Algorithms?

  • In the field of Computer Science, everything is related to databases.
  • When we talk about a database that contains various columns, sorting algorithms are needed to arrange the data in a particular order (increasing/ decreasing).
  • Sorting is an important category of algorithms in the field of Computer Science and a lot of research is still going on.
  • Categories of Sorting Algorithms Sorting algorithms are generally compared on the following parameters: 1.

12.3 Categories of Sorting Algorithms

  • Sorting algorithms are generally compared on the following parameters: 1.
  • Number of Comparisons The most important parameter to judge a sorting algorithm is the number of comparisons done to sort a given list of items.
  • The comparison sorting algorithms consists of merge sort, quick sort, bubble, insertion, and selection sort.
  • Whereas, non-comparison sorting algorithms consist of count sort, bucket sort, and radix sort.

12.4 Bubble Sort

  • Bubble sort is the simplest algorithm that works by comparing each pair of elements and swapping elements if they are in the wrong order.
  • The algorithm continues iteration until no more swaps are required.
  • The largest element goes to the end of array after first pass.
  • The second largest element goes to second last position after second pass and so on.

12.5 Selection Sort

  • Selection sort works by repeatedly selecting the smallest element from the unsorted Sorted Array Sorted Array 76 array and swapping it with the first unsorted element.
  • The process continues till the array is sorted.
  • The algorithm is easy to understand and does not require additional memory space for sorting.
  • Find the minimum element in the unsorted array and swap it with element at current position.

12.6 Insertion Sort

  • It is a simple sorting algorithm that divide the array into two parts i.e., sorted and unsorted.
  • The algorithm works by iteratively inserting each element of unsorted list into the right place in the sorted list.
  • The first element of the array is assured to be sorted.
  • Compare the second element with the element in the sorted array if it is smaller than swap.

12.7 Merge Sort

  • Merge sort is popular sorting algorithm that works on Divide and Conquer strategy.
  • It works by recursively dividing i/p array into two halves, sorting both halves and merging them together to obtain sorted array.
  • Divide the unsorted array into parts until it cannot be sub-divided- Divide 2.
  • Conquer each sub-array created and sort them – Conquer Note – If an array contains single element, it is considered sorted.

12.8 Quick Sort

  • Quick sort works on divide and conquer strategy and is also known as partition exchange sort.
  • Just like merge sort, it uses recursive calls to sort the array.
  • The algorithm picks an element as a pivot and partitions the unsorted array around pivot with an aim of placing pivot in the correct position in the sorted array.
  • It is in-place algorithm that do not require auxiliary space for sorting.

12.9 Comparing Various Sorting Algorithms

  • In this section, we will discuss best, average, and worst case time complexity of various sorting algorithms.
  • Let’s understand this with help of an example: 1.
  • List.sort() Given a list of numbers, it sorts the list in ascending or descending order without using any additional space.
  • It makes changes in the original list and does not return a new list.
